content.english: ℣. O Lord, + open thou my lips.

content.latin: ℟. Et os meum annuntiábit laudem tuam.
content.english: ℟. And my mouth shall declare thy praise.

content.latin: ℣. Deus ✠ in adiutórium meum inténde.
content.english: ℣. O God, ✠ come to my assistance;

content.latin: ℟. Dómine, ad adiuvándum me festína.
content.english: ℟. O Lord, make haste to help me.

content.latin: Ant. Regem Confessórum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. The Lord, the King of Confessors, * O come, let us worship.

content.latin: Ant. Regem Confessórum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. The Lord, the King of Confessors, * O come, let us worship.

content.latin: Veníte, exsultémus Dómino, iubilémus Deo, salutári nostro: præoccupémus fáciem eius in confessióne, et in psalmis iubilémus ei.
content.english: Come let us praise the Lord with joy: let us joyfully sing to God our saviour. Let us come before his presence with thanksgiving; and make a joyful noise to him with psalms.

content.latin: Ant. Regem Confessórum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. The Lord, the King of Confessors, * O come, let us worship.

content.latin: Quóniam Deus magnus Dóminus, et Rex magnus super omnes deos, quóniam non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: quia in manu eius sunt omnes fines terræ, et altitúdines móntium ipse cónspicit.
content.english: For the Lord is a great God, and a great King above all gods. For the Lord will not cast off his people: for in his hand are all the ends of the earth, and the heights of the mountains are his.

content.latin: Ant. Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. O come, let us worship.

content.latin: Quóniam ipsíus est mare, et ipse fecit illud, et áridam fundavérunt manus eius (genuflectitur) veníte, adorémus, et procidámus ante Deum: plorémus coram Dómino, qui fecit nos, quia ipse est Dóminus, Deus noster; nos autem pópulus eius, et oves páscuæ eius.
content.english: For the sea is his, and he made it: and his hands formed the dry land. (genuflect) Come let us adore and fall down: and weep before the Lord that made us: For he is the Lord our God: and we are the people of his pasture and the sheep of his hand.

content.latin: Ant. Regem Confessórum Dóminum, * Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. The Lord, the King of Confessors, * O come, let us worship.

content.latin: Hódie, si vocem eius audiéritis, nolíte obduráre corda vestra, sicut in exacerbatióne secúndum diem tentatiónis in desérto: ubi tentavérunt me patres vestri, probavérunt et vidérunt ópera mea.
content.english: Today if you shall hear his voice, harden not your hearts: As in the provocation, according to the day of temptation in the wilderness: where your fathers tempted me, they proved me, and saw my works.

content.latin: Ant. Veníte, adorémus.
content.english: Ant. O come, let us worship.

content.latin: Quadragínta annis próximus fui generatióni huic, et dixi: Semper hi errant corde, ipsi vero non cognovérunt vias meas: quibus iurávi in ira mea: Si introíbunt in réquiem meam.
content.english: Forty years long was I offended with that generation, and I said: These always err in heart. And these men have not known my ways: so I swore in my wrath that they shall not enter into my rest.

content.latin: Iste Conféssor Dómini, coléntes
content.english: This the confessor of the Lord, whose triumph

content.latin: Quem pie laudant pópuli per orbem,
content.english: Now all the faithful celebrate, with gladness

content.latin: Hac die lætus méruit suprémos
content.english: On this feast day year by year receiveth

content.latin: Laudis honóres.
content.english: Merited honors.

content.latin: Qui pius, prudens, húmilis, pudícus,
content.english: Saintly and prudent, modest in behaviour,

content.latin: Sóbriam duxit sine labe vitam,
content.english: Peaceful and sober, chaste was he, and lowly.

content.latin: Donec humános animávit auræ
content.english: While that life’s vigour, coursing through his members,

content.latin: Spíritus artus.
content.english: Quickened his being.

content.latin: Cuius ob præstans méritum, frequénter,
content.english: Sick ones of old time, to his tomb resorting,

content.latin: Ægra quæ passim iacuére membra,
content.english: Sorely by ailments manifold afflicted,

content.latin: Víribus morbi dómitis, salúti
content.english: Oft-times have welcomed health and strength returning,

content.latin: Restituúntur.
content.english: At his petition.

content.latin: Noster hinc illi chorus obsequéntem
content.english: Whence we in chorus gladly do him honour,

content.latin: Cóncinit laudem celebrésque palmas,
content.english: Chanting his praises with devout affection,

content.latin: Ut piis eius précibus iuvémur
content.english: That in his merits we may have a portion,

content.latin: Omne per ævum.
content.english: Now and forever.

content.latin: Sit salus illi, decus atque virtus,
content.english: His be the glory, power and salvation,

content.latin: Qui, super cæli sólio corúscans,
content.english: Who over all things reigneth in the highest,

content.latin: Tótius mundi sériem gubérnat,
content.english: Earth’s mighty fabric ruling and directing,

content.latin: Trinus et unus.
content.english: Onely and Trinal.

content.latin: Amen.
content.english: Amen.

content.english: At the Nocturn

content.latin: Ant. Memor fuit in sǽculum * testaménti sui Dóminus Deus noster.
content.english: Ant. The memory of thy testament * will live forever, O Lord our God.

content.latin: 104:1 Confitémini Dómino, et invocáte nomen eius: * annuntiáte inter gentes ópera eius.
content.english: 104:1 Give glory to the Lord, and call upon his name: * declare his deeds among the Gentiles.

content.latin: 104:2 Cantáte ei, et psállite ei: * narráte ómnia mirabília eius.
content.english: 104:2 Sing to him, yea sing praises to him: * relate all his wondrous works.

content.latin: 104:3 Laudámini in nómine sancto eius: * lætétur cor quæréntium Dóminum.
content.english: 104:3 Glory ye in his holy name: * let the heart of them rejoice that seek the Lord.

content.latin: 104:4 Quǽrite Dóminum, et confirmámini: * quǽrite fáciem eius semper.
content.english: 104:4 Seek ye the Lord, and be strengthened: * seek his face evermore.

content.latin: 104:5 Mementóte mirabílium eius, quæ fecit: * prodígia eius, et iudícia oris eius.
content.english: 104:5 Remember his marvellous works which he hath done; * his wonders, and the judgments of his mouth.

content.latin: 104:6 Semen Ábraham, servi eius: * fílii Iacob, elécti eius.
content.english: 104:6 O ye seed of Abraham his servant; * ye sons of Jacob his chosen.

content.latin: 104:7 Ipse Dóminus Deus noster: * in univérsa terra iudícia eius.
content.english: 104:7 He is the Lord our God: * his judgments are in all the earth.

content.latin: 104:8 Memor fuit in sǽculum testaménti sui: * verbi, quod mandávit in mille generatiónes:
content.english: 104:8 He hath remembered his covenant for ever: * the word which he commanded to a thousand generations.

content.latin: 104:9 Quod dispósuit ad Ábraham: * et iuraménti sui ad Isaac:
content.english: 104:9 Which he made to Abraham; * and his oath to Isaac:

content.latin: 104:10 Et státuit illud Iacob in præcéptum: * et Israël in testaméntum ætérnum:
content.english: 104:10 And he appointed the same to Jacob for a law, * and to Israel for an everlasting testament:

content.latin: 104:11 Dicens: Tibi dabo terram Chánaan, * funículum hereditátis vestræ.
content.english: 104:11 Saying: To thee will I give the land of Chanaan, * the lot of your inheritance.

content.latin: 104:12 Cum essent número brevi, * paucíssimi et íncolæ eius:
content.english: 104:12 When they were but a small number: * yea very few, and sojourners therein:

content.latin: 104:13 Et pertransiérunt de gente in gentem, * et de regno ad pópulum álterum.
content.english: 104:13 And they passed from nation to nation, * and from one kingdom to another people.

content.latin: 104:14 Non relíquit hóminem nocére eis: * et corrípuit pro eis reges.
content.english: 104:14 He suffered no man to hurt them: * and he reproved kings for their sakes.

content.latin: 104:15 Nolíte tángere christos meos: * et in prophétis meis nolíte malignári.
content.english: 104:15 Touch ye not my anointed: * and do no evil to my prophets.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Memor fuit in sǽculum testaménti sui Dóminus Deus noster.
content.english: Ant. The memory of thy testament will live forever, O Lord our God.

content.latin: Ant. Auxit Dóminus * pópulum suum: et firmávit eum super inimícos eius.
content.english: Ant. The Lord increased his people exceedingly * and strengthened them over their enemies.

content.latin: 104:16 Et vocávit famem super terram: * et omne firmaméntum panis contrívit.
content.english: 104:16 And he called a famine upon the land: * and he broke in pieces all the support of bread.

content.latin: 104:17 Misit ante eos virum: * in servum venúmdatus est Ioseph.
content.english: 104:17 He sent a man before them: * Joseph, who was sold for a slave.

content.latin: 104:18 Humiliavérunt in compédibus pedes eius, ferrum pertránsiit ánimam eius * donec veníret verbum eius.
content.english: 104:18 They humbled his feet in fetters: the iron pierced his soul, * until his word came.

content.latin: 104:19 Elóquium Dómini inflammávit eum: * misit rex, et solvit eum; princeps populórum, et dimísit eum.
content.english: 104:19 The word of the Lord inflamed him: * the king sent, and he released him: the ruler of the people, and he set him at liberty.

content.latin: 104:21 Constítuit eum dóminum domus suæ: * et príncipem omnis possessiónis suæ:
content.english: 104:21 He made him master of his house, * and ruler of all his possession.

content.latin: 104:22 Ut erudíret príncipes eius sicut semetípsum: * et senes eius prudéntiam docéret.
content.english: 104:22 That he might instruct his princes as himself, * and teach his ancients wisdom.

content.latin: 104:23 Et intrávit Israël in Ægýptum: * et Iacob áccola fuit in terra Cham.
content.english: 104:23 And Israel went into Egypt: * and Jacob was a sojourner in the land of Cham.

content.latin: 104:24 Et auxit pópulum suum veheménter: * et firmávit eum super inimícos eius.
content.english: 104:24 And he increased his people exceedingly: * and strengthened them over their enemies,

content.latin: 104:25 Convértit cor eórum ut odírent pópulum eius: * et dolum fácerent in servos eius.
content.english: 104:25 He turned their heart to hate his people: * and to deal deceitfully with his servants.

content.latin: 104:26 Misit Móysen, servum suum: * Aaron, quem elégit ipsum.
content.english: 104:26 He sent Moses his servant: * Aaron the man whom he had chosen.

content.latin: 104:27 Pósuit in eis verba signórum suórum: * et prodigiórum in terra Cham.
content.english: 104:27 He gave them power to shew his signs, * and his wonders in the land of Cham.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Auxit Dóminus pópulum suum: et firmávit eum super inimícos eius.
content.english: Ant. The Lord increased his people exceedingly and strengthened them over their enemies.

content.latin: Ant. Edúxit Deus * pópulum suum in exsultatióne, et eléctos suos in lætítia.
content.english: Ant. The Lord brought forth * his people with joy, and his chosen with gladness.

content.latin: 104:28 Misit ténebras, et obscurávit: * et non exacerbávit sermónes suos.
content.english: 104:28 He sent darkness, and made it obscure: * and grieved not his words.

content.latin: 104:29 Convértit aquas eórum in sánguinem: * et occídit pisces eórum.
content.english: 104:29 He turned their waters into blood, * and destroyed their fish.

content.latin: 104:30 Édidit terra eórum ranas: * in penetrálibus regum ipsórum.
content.english: 104:30 Their land brought forth frogs, * in the inner chambers of their kings.

content.latin: 104:31 Dixit, et venit cœnomyía: * et cínifes in ómnibus fínibus eórum.
content.english: 104:31 He spoke, and there came diverse sorts of flies, * and sciniphs in all their coasts.

content.latin: 104:32 Pósuit plúvias eórum grándinem: * ignem comburéntem in terra ipsórum.
content.english: 104:32 He gave them hail for rain, * a burning fire in the land.

content.latin: 104:33 Et percússit víneas eórum, et ficúlneas eórum: * et contrívit lignum fínium eórum.
content.english: 104:33 And he destroyed their vineyards, and their fig trees: * and he broke in pieces the trees of their coasts.

content.latin: 104:34 Dixit, et venit locústa, et bruchus, * cuius non erat númerus:
content.english: 104:34 He spoke, and the locust came, and the bruchus, * of which there was no number.

content.latin: 104:35 Et comédit omne fænum in terra eórum: * et comédit omnem fructum terræ eórum.
content.english: 104:35 And they devoured all the grass in their land, * and consumed all the fruit of their ground.

content.latin: 104:36 Et percússit omne primogénitum in terra eórum: * primítias omnis labóris eórum.
content.english: 104:36 And he slew all the firstborn in their land: * the firstfruits of all their labour.

content.latin: 104:37 Et edúxit eos cum argénto et auro: * et non erat in tríbubus eórum infírmus.
content.english: 104:37 And he brought them out with silver and gold: * and there was not among their tribes one that was feeble.

content.latin: 104:38 Lætáta est Ægýptus in profectióne eórum: * quia incúbuit timor eórum super eos.
content.english: 104:38 Egypt was glad when they departed: * for the fear of them lay upon them.

content.latin: 104:39 Expándit nubem in protectiónem eórum: * et ignem ut lucéret eis per noctem.
content.english: 104:39 He spread a cloud for their protection, * and fire to give them light in the night.

content.latin: 104:40 Petiérunt, et venit cotúrnix: * et pane cæli saturávit eos.
content.english: 104:40 They asked, and the quail came: * and he filled them with the bread of heaven.

content.latin: 104:41 Dirúpit petram et fluxérunt aquæ: * abiérunt in sicco flúmina;
content.english: 104:41 He opened the rock, and waters flowed: * rivers ran down in the dry land.

content.latin: 104:42 Quóniam memor fuit verbi sancti sui: * quod hábuit ad Ábraham, púerum suum.
content.english: 104:42 Because he remembered his holy word, * which he had spoken to his servant Abraham.

content.latin: 104:43 Et edúxit pópulum suum in exsultatióne, * et eléctos suos in lætítia.
content.english: 104:43 And he brought forth his people with joy, * and his chosen with gladness.

content.latin: 104:44 Et dedit illis regiónes géntium: * et labóres populórum possedérunt:
content.english: 104:44 And he gave them the lands of the Gentiles: * and they possessed the labours of the people:

content.latin: 104:45 Ut custódiant iustificatiónes eius, * et legem eius requírant.
content.english: 104:45 That they might observe his justifications, * and seek after his law.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Edúxit Deus pópulum suum in exsultatióne, et eléctos suos in lætítia.
content.english: Ant. The Lord brought forth his people with joy, and his chosen with gladness.

content.latin: Ant. Salvávit eos Dóminus * propter nomen suum.
content.english: Ant. The Lord saved them * for his own name's sake.

content.latin: 105:1 Confitémini Dómino, quóniam bonus: * quóniam in sǽculum misericórdia eius.
content.english: 105:1 Give glory to the Lord, for he is good: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

content.latin: 105:2 Quis loquétur poténtias Dómini, * audítas fáciet omnes laudes eius?
content.english: 105:2 Who shall declare the powers of the Lord? * who shall set forth all his praises?

content.latin: 105:3 Beáti, qui custódiunt iudícium, * et fáciunt iustítiam in omni témpore.
content.english: 105:3 Blessed are they that keep judgment, * and do justice at all times.

content.latin: 105:4 Meménto nostri, Dómine, in beneplácito pópuli tui: * vísita nos in salutári tuo:
content.english: 105:4 Remember us, O Lord, in the favour of thy people: * visit us with thy salvation.

content.latin: 105:5 Ad vidéndum in bonitáte electórum tuórum, ad lætándum in lætítia gentis tuæ: * ut laudéris cum hereditáte tua.
content.english: 105:5 That we may see the good of thy chosen, that we may rejoice in the joy of thy nation: * that thou mayst be praised with thy inheritance.

content.latin: 105:6 Peccávimus cum pátribus nostris: * iniúste égimus, iniquitátem fécimus.
content.english: 105:6 We have sinned with our fathers: * we have acted unjustly, we have wrought iniquity.

content.latin: 105:7 Patres nostri in Ægýpto non intellexérunt mirabília tua: * non fuérunt mémores multitúdinis misericórdiæ tuæ.
content.english: 105:7 Our fathers understood not thy wonders in Egypt: * they remembered not the multitude of thy mercies:

content.latin: 105:7 Et irritavérunt ascendéntes in mare, * Mare Rubrum.
content.english: 105:7 And they provoked to wrath going up to the sea, * even the Red Sea.

content.latin: 105:8 Et salvávit eos propter nomen suum: * ut notam fáceret poténtiam suam.
content.english: 105:8 And he saved them for his own name’s sake: * that he might make his power known.

content.latin: 105:9 Et incrépuit Mare Rubrum, et exsiccátum est, * et dedúxit eos in abýssis sicut in desérto.
content.english: 105:9 And he rebuked the Red Sea, and it was dried up: * and he led them through the depths, as in a wilderness.

content.latin: 105:10 Et salvávit eos de manu odiéntium: * et redémit eos de manu inimíci.
content.english: 105:10 And he saved them from the hand of them that hated them: * and he redeemed them from the hand of the enemy.

content.latin: 105:11 Et opéruit aqua tribulántes eos: * unus ex eis non remánsit.
content.english: 105:11 And the water covered them that afflicted them: * there was not one of them left.

content.latin: 105:12 Et credidérunt verbis eius: * et laudavérunt laudem eius.
content.english: 105:12 And they believed his words: * and they sang his praises.

content.latin: 105:13 Cito fecérunt, oblíti sunt óperum eius: * et non sustinuérunt consílium eius.
content.english: 105:13 They had quickly done, they forgot his works: * and they waited not for his counsels.

content.latin: 105:14 Et concupiérunt concupiscéntiam in desérto: * et tentavérunt Deum in inaquóso.
content.english: 105:14 And they coveted their desire in the desert: * and they tempted God in the place without water.

content.latin: 105:15 Et dedit eis petitiónem ipsórum: * et misit saturitátem in ánimas eórum.
content.english: 105:15 And he gave them their request: * and sent fulness into their souls.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Salvávit eos Dóminus propter nomen suum.
content.english: Ant. The Lord saved them for his own name's sake.

content.latin: Ant. Oblíti sunt Deum * qui salvávit eos.
content.english: Ant. They forgot God * who saved them.

content.latin: 105:16 Et irritavérunt Móysen in castris: * Aaron, sanctum Dómini.
content.english: 105:16 And they provoked Moses in the camp, * Aaron the holy one of the Lord.

content.latin: 105:17 Apérta est terra, et deglutívit Dathan: * et opéruit super congregatiónem Abíron.
content.english: 105:17 The earth opened and swallowed up Dathan: * and covered the congregation of Abiron.

content.latin: 105:18 Et exársit ignis in synagóga eórum * flamma combússit peccatóres.
content.english: 105:18 And a fire was kindled in their congregation: * the flame burned the wicked.

content.latin: 105:19 Et fecérunt vítulum in Horeb * et adoravérunt scúlptile.
content.english: 105:19 They made also a calf in Horeb: * and they adored the graven thing.

content.latin: 105:20 Et mutavérunt glóriam suam * in similitúdinem vítuli comedéntis fænum.
content.english: 105:20 And they changed their glory * into the likeness of a calf that eateth grass.

content.latin: 105:21 Oblíti sunt Deum, qui salvávit eos, * qui fecit magnália in Ægýpto, mirabília in terra Cham: terribília in Mari Rubro.
content.english: 105:21 They forgot God, who saved them, * who had done great things in Egypt, wondrous works in the land of Cham: terrible things in the Red Sea.

content.latin: 105:23 Et dixit ut dispérderet eos: * si non Móyses, eléctus eius, stetísset in confractióne in conspéctu eius:
content.english: 105:23 And he said that he would destroy them: * had not Moses his chosen stood before him in the breach:

content.latin: 105:24 Ut avérteret iram eius ne dispérderet eos: * et pro níhilo habuérunt terram desiderábilem:
content.english: 105:24 To turn away his wrath, lest he should destroy them; * and they set at nought the desirable land.

content.latin: 105:25 Non credidérunt verbo eius, et murmuravérunt in tabernáculis suis: * non exaudiérunt vocem Dómini.
content.english: 105:25 They believed not his word, and they murmured in their tents: * they hearkened not to the voice of the Lord.

content.latin: 105:26 Et elevávit manum suam super eos: * ut prostérneret eos in desérto:
content.english: 105:26 And he lifted up his hand over them: * to overthrow them in the desert;

content.latin: 105:27 Et ut deíceret semen eórum in natiónibus: * et dispérgeret eos in regiónibus.
content.english: 105:27 And to cast down their seed among the nations, * and to scatter them in the countries.

content.latin: 105:28 Et initiáti sunt Beélphegor: * et comedérunt sacrifícia mortuórum.
content.english: 105:28 They also were initiated to Beelphegor: * and ate the sacrifices of the dead.

content.latin: 105:29 Et irritavérunt eum in adinventiónibus suis: * et multiplicáta est in eis ruína.
content.english: 105:29 And they provoked him with their inventions: * and destruction was multiplied among them.

content.latin: 105:30 Et stetit Phínees, et placávit: * et cessávit quassátio.
content.english: 105:30 Then Phinees stood up, and pacified him: * and the slaughter ceased.

content.latin: 105:31 Et reputátum est ei in iustítiam: * in generatiónem et generatiónem usque in sempitérnum.
content.english: 105:31 And it was reputed to him unto justice, * to generation and generation for evermore.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Oblíti sunt Deum qui salvávit eos.
content.english: Ant. They forgot God who saved them.

content.latin: Ant. Cum tribularéntur * vidit Dóminus: et audívit oratiónem eórum.
content.english: Ant. And he saw when they were in tribulation * and he heard their prayer.

content.latin: 105:32 Et irritavérunt eum ad aquas contradictiónis: * et vexátus est Móyses propter eos: quia exacerbavérunt spíritum eius.
content.english: 105:32 They provoked him also at the waters of contradiction: * and Moses was afflicted for their sakes: because they exasperated his spirit.

content.latin: 105:33 Et distínxit in lábiis suis: * non disperdidérunt gentes, quas dixit Dóminus illis.
content.english: 105:33 And he distinguished with his lips; * they did not destroy the nations of which the Lord spoke unto them.

content.latin: 105:35 Et commísti sunt inter gentes, et didicérunt ópera eórum: et serviérunt sculptílibus eórum: * et factum est illis in scándalum.
content.english: 105:35 And they were mingled among the heathens, and learned their works: and served their idols, * and it became a stumblingblock to them.

content.latin: 105:37 Et immolavérunt fílios suos, * et fílias suas dæmóniis.
content.english: 105:37 And they sacrificed their sons, * and their daughters to devils.

content.latin: 105:38 Et effudérunt sánguinem innocéntem: * sánguinem filiórum suórum et filiárum suárum, quas sacrificavérunt sculptílibus Chánaan.
content.english: 105:38 And they shed innocent blood: * the blood of their sons and of their daughters which they sacrificed to the idols of Chanaan.

content.latin: 105:39 Et infécta est terra in sanguínibus, et contamináta est in opéribus eórum: * et fornicáti sunt in adinventiónibus suis.
content.english: 105:39 And the land was polluted with blood, and was defiled with their works: * and they went aside after their own inventions.

content.latin: 105:40 Et irátus est furóre Dóminus in pópulum suum: * et abominátus est hereditátem suam.
content.english: 105:40 And the Lord was exceedingly angry with his people: * and he abhorred his inheritance.

content.latin: 105:41 Et trádidit eos in manus géntium: * et domináti sunt eórum qui odérunt eos.
content.english: 105:41 And he delivered them into the hands of the nations: * and they that hated them had dominion over them.

content.latin: 105:42 Et tribulavérunt eos inimíci eórum, et humiliáti sunt sub mánibus eórum: * sæpe liberávit eos.
content.english: 105:42 And their enemies afflicted them: and they were humbled under their hands: * many times did he deliver them.

content.latin: 105:43 Ipsi autem exacerbavérunt eum in consílio suo: * et humiliáti sunt in iniquitátibus suis.
content.english: 105:43 But they provoked him with their counsel: * and they were brought low by their iniquities.

content.latin: 105:44 Et vidit, cum tribularéntur: * et audívit oratiónem eórum.
content.english: 105:44 And he saw when they were in tribulation: * and he heard their prayer.

content.latin: 105:45 Et memor fuit testaménti sui: * et pœnítuit eum secúndum multitúdinem misericórdiæ suæ.
content.english: 105:45 And he was mindful of his covenant: * and repented according to the multitude of his mercies.

content.latin: 105:46 Et dedit eos in misericórdias * in conspéctu ómnium qui céperant eos.
content.english: 105:46 And he gave them unto mercies, * in the sight of all those that had made them captives.

content.latin: 105:47 Salvos nos fac, Dómine, Deus noster: * et cóngrega nos de natiónibus:
content.english: 105:47 Save us, O Lord, our God: * and gather us from among nations:

content.latin: 105:47 Ut confiteámur nómini sancto tuo: * et gloriémur in laude tua.
content.english: 105:47 That we may give thanks to thy holy name, * and may glory in thy praise.

content.latin: 105:48 Benedíctus Dóminus, Deus Israël, a sǽculo et usque in sǽculum: * et dicet omnis pópulus: Fiat, fiat.
content.english: 105:48 Blessed be the Lord the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting: * and let all the people say: So be it, so be it.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Cum tribularéntur vidit Dóminus: et audívit oratiónem eórum.
content.english: Ant. And he saw when they were in tribulation and he heard their prayer.

content.latin: Ant. Clamavérunt ad Dóminum * et de necessitátibus eórum liberávit eos.
content.english: Ant. Then they cried to the Lord * and he delivered them out of their distresses.

content.latin: 106:1 Confitémini Dómino quóniam bonus: * quóniam in sǽculum misericórdia eius.
content.english: 106:1 Give glory to the Lord, for he is good: * for his mercy endureth for ever.

content.latin: 106:2 Dicant qui redémpti sunt a Dómino, quos redémit de manu inimíci: * et de regiónibus congregávit eos:
content.english: 106:2 Let them say so that have been redeemed by the Lord, whom he hath redeemed from the hand of the enemy: * and gathered out of the countries.

content.latin: 106:3 A solis ortu, et occásu: * ab aquilóne, et mari.
content.english: 106:3 From the rising and the setting of the sun, * from the north and from the sea.

content.latin: 106:4 Erravérunt in solitúdine in inaquóso: * viam civitátis habitáculi non invenérunt.
content.english: 106:4 They wandered in a wilderness, in a place without water: * they found not the way of a city for their habitation.

content.latin: 106:5 Esuriéntes, et sitiéntes: * ánima eórum in ipsis defécit.
content.english: 106:5 They were hungry and thirsty: * their soul fainted in them.

content.latin: 106:6 Et clamavérunt ad Dóminum cum tribularéntur: * et de necessitátibus eórum erípuit eos.
content.english: 106:6 And they cried to the Lord in their tribulation: * and he delivered them out of their distresses.

content.latin: 106:7 Et dedúxit eos in viam rectam: * ut irent in civitátem habitatiónis.
content.english: 106:7 And he led them into the right way: * that they might go to a city of habitation.

content.latin: 106:8 Confiteántur Dómino misericórdiæ eius: * et mirabília eius fíliis hóminum.
content.english: 106:8 Let the mercies of the Lord give glory to him: * and his wonderful works to the children of men.

content.latin: 106:9 Quia satiávit ánimam inánem: * et ánimam esuriéntem satiávit bonis.
content.english: 106:9 For he hath satisfied the empty soul, * and hath filled the hungry soul with good things.

content.latin: 106:10 Sedéntes in ténebris, et umbra mortis: * vinctos in mendicitáte et ferro.
content.english: 106:10 Such as sat in darkness and in the shadow of death: * bound in want and in iron.

content.latin: 106:11 Quia exacerbavérunt elóquia Dei: * et consílium Altíssimi irritavérunt.
content.english: 106:11 Because they had exasperated the words of God: * and provoked the counsel of the most High:

content.latin: 106:12 Et humiliátum est in labóribus cor eórum: * infirmáti sunt, nec fuit qui adiuváret.
content.english: 106:12 And their heart was humbled with labours: * they were weakened, and there was none to help them.

content.latin: 106:13 Et clamavérunt ad Dóminum cum tribularéntur: * et de necessitátibus eórum liberávit eos.
content.english: 106:13 Then they cried to the Lord in their affliction: * and he delivered them out of their distresses.

content.latin: 106:14 Et edúxit eos de ténebris, et umbra mortis: * et víncula eórum disrúpit.
content.english: 106:14 And he brought them out of darkness, * and the shadow of death; and broke their bonds in sunder.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Clamavérunt ad Dóminum et de necessitátibus eórum liberávit eos.
content.english: Ant. Then they cried to the Lord and he delivered them out of their distresses.

content.latin: Ant. Ipsi vidérunt * ópera Dei et mirabília eius.
content.english: Ant. These have seen * the works of the Lord, and his wonders.

content.latin: 106:15 Confiteántur Dómino misericórdiæ eius: * et mirabília eius fíliis hóminum.
content.english: 106:15 Let the mercies of the Lord give glory to him, * and his wonderful works to the children of men.

content.latin: 106:16 Quia contrívit portas ǽreas: * et vectes férreos confrégit.
content.english: 106:16 Because he hath broken gates of brass, * and burst the iron bars.

content.latin: 106:17 Suscépit eos de via iniquitátis eórum: * propter iniustítias enim suas humiliáti sunt.
content.english: 106:17 He took them out of the way of their iniquity: * for they were brought low for their injustices.

content.latin: 106:18 Omnem escam abomináta est ánima eórum: * et appropinquavérunt usque ad portas mortis.
content.english: 106:18 Their soul abhorred all manner of meat: * and they drew nigh even to the gates of death.

content.latin: 106:19 Et clamavérunt ad Dóminum cum tribularéntur: * et de necessitátibus eórum liberávit eos.
content.english: 106:19 And they cried to the Lord in their affliction: * and he delivered them out of their distresses.

content.latin: 106:20 Misit verbum suum, et sanávit eos: * et erípuit eos de interitiónibus eórum.
content.english: 106:20 He sent his word, and healed them: * and delivered them from their destructions.

content.latin: 106:21 Confiteántur Dómino misericórdiæ eius: * et mirabília eius fíliis hóminum.
content.english: 106:21 Let the mercies of the Lord give glory to him: * and his wonderful works to the children of men

content.latin: 106:22 Et sacríficent sacrifícium laudis: * et annúntient ópera eius in exsultatióne.
content.english: 106:22 And let them sacrifice the sacrifice of praise: * and declare his works with joy.

content.latin: 106:23 Qui descéndunt mare in návibus, * faciéntes operatiónem in aquis multis.
content.english: 106:23 They that go down to the sea in ships, * doing business in the great waters:

content.latin: 106:24 Ipsi vidérunt ópera Dómini, * et mirabília eius in profúndo.
content.english: 106:24 These have seen the works of the Lord, * and his wonders in the deep.

content.latin: 106:25 Dixit, et stetit spíritus procéllæ: * et exaltáti sunt fluctus eius.
content.english: 106:25 He said the word, and there arose a storm of wind: * and the waves thereof were lifted up.

content.latin: 106:26 Ascéndunt usque ad cælos, et descéndunt usque ad abýssos: * ánima eórum in malis tabescébat.
content.english: 106:26 They mount up to the heavens, and they go down to the depths: * their soul pined away with evils.

content.latin: 106:27 Turbáti sunt, et moti sunt sicut ébrius: * et omnis sapiéntia eórum devoráta est.
content.english: 106:27 They were troubled, and reeled like a drunken man; * and all their wisdom was swallowed up.

content.latin: 106:28 Et clamavérunt ad Dóminum cum tribularéntur: * et de necessitátibus eórum edúxit eos.
content.english: 106:28 And they cried to the Lord in their affliction: * and he brought them out of their distresses.

content.latin: 106:29 Et státuit procéllam eius in auram: * et siluérunt fluctus eius.
content.english: 106:29 And he turned the storm into a breeze: * and its waves were still.

content.latin: 106:30 Et lætáti sunt quia siluérunt: * et dedúxit eos in portum voluntátis eórum.
content.english: 106:30 And they rejoiced because they were still: * and he brought them to the haven which they wished for.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Ipsi vidérunt ópera Dei et mirabília eius.
content.english: Ant. These have seen the works of the Lord, and his wonders.

content.latin: Ant. Vidébunt recti * et lætabúntur, et intéllegent misericórdias Dómini.
content.english: Ant. The just see and rejoice * and understand the mercy of the Lord.

content.latin: 106:31 Confiteántur Dómino misericórdiæ eius: * et mirabília eius fíliis hóminum.
content.english: 106:31 Let the mercies of the Lord give glory to him, * and his wonderful works to the children of men.

content.latin: 106:32 Et exáltent eum in ecclésia plebis: * et in cáthedra seniórum laudent eum.
content.english: 106:32 And let them exalt him in the church of the people: * and praise him in the chair of the ancients.

content.latin: 106:33 Pósuit flúmina in desértum: * et éxitus aquárum in sitim.
content.english: 106:33 He hath turned rivers into a wilderness: * and the sources of water into dry ground:

content.latin: 106:34 Terram fructíferam in salsúginem: * a malítia inhabitántium in ea.
content.english: 106:34 A fruitful land into barrenness, * for the wickedness of them that dwell therein.

content.latin: 106:35 Pósuit desértum in stagna aquárum: * et terram sine aqua in éxitus aquárum.
content.english: 106:35 He hath turned a wilderness into pools of water, * and a dry land into water springs.

content.latin: 106:36 Et collocávit illic esuriéntes: * et constituérunt civitátem habitatiónis.
content.english: 106:36 And hath placed there the hungry; * and they made a city for their habitation.

content.latin: 106:37 Et seminavérunt agros, et plantavérunt víneas: * et fecérunt fructum nativitátis.
content.english: 106:37 And they sowed fields, and planted vineyards: * and they yielded fruit of birth.

content.latin: 106:38 Et benedíxit eis, et multiplicáti sunt nimis: * et iuménta eórum non minorávit.
content.english: 106:38 And he blessed them, and they were multiplied exceedingly: * and their cattle he suffered not to decrease.

content.latin: 106:39 Et pauci facti sunt: * et vexáti sunt a tribulatióne malórum, et dolóre.
content.english: 106:39 Then they were brought to be few: * and they were afflicted through the trouble of evils and sorrow.

content.latin: 106:40 Effúsa est contémptio super príncipes: * et erráre fecit eos in ínvio, et non in via.
content.english: 106:40 Contempt was poured forth upon their princes: *and he caused them to wander where there was no passing, and out of the way.

content.latin: 106:41 Et adiúvit páuperem de inópia: * et pósuit sicut oves famílias.
content.english: 106:41 And he helped the poor out of poverty: * and made him families like a flock of sheep.

content.latin: 106:42 Vidébunt recti, et lætabúntur: * et omnis iníquitas oppilábit os suum.
content.english: 106:42 The just shall see, and shall rejoice, * and all iniquity shall stop their mouth.

content.latin: 106:43 Quis sápiens et custódiet hæc? * et intélleget misericórdias Dómini.
content.english: 106:43 Who is wise, and will keep these things: * and will understand the mercies of the Lord?

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: Ant. Vidébunt recti et lætabúntur, et intéllegent misericórdias Dómini.
content.english: Ant. The just see and rejoice and understand the mercy of the Lord.

content.latin: ℣. Exáltent Dóminum in ecclésia plebis.
content.english: ℣. Let them exalt the Lord in the church of the people.

content.latin: ℟. Et in cáthedra seniórum laudent eum.
content.english: ℟. And praise him in the chair of the ancients.

content.latin: Pater Noster dicitur secreto usque ad Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: Our Father is said silently until And lead us not into temptation:.

content.latin: Pater noster, qui es in cælis, sanctificétur nomen tuum: advéniat regnum tuum: fiat volúntas tua, sicut in cælo et in terra. Panem nostrum cotidiánum da nobis hódie: et dimítte nobis débita nostra, sicut et nos dimíttimus debitóribus nostris:
content.english: Our Father, who art in heaven, Hallowed be thy name. Thy kingdom come. Thy will be done on earth as it is in heaven. Give us this day our daily bread. And forgive us our trespasses, as we forgive those who trespass against us.

content.latin: ℣. Et ne nos indúcas in tentatiónem:
content.english: ℣. And lead us not into temptation:

content.latin: ℟. Sed líbera nos a malo.
content.english: ℟. But deliver us from evil.

content.latin: Absolutio. A vínculis peccatórum nostrórum absólvat nos omnípotens et miséricors Dóminus.
content.english: Absolution. May the Almighty and merciful Lord loose us from the bonds of our sins.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

content.latin: Benedictio. Ille nos benedícat, qui sine fine vivit et regnat.
content.english: Benediction. May His blessing be upon us who doth live and reign for ever.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.latin: De libro tértio Regum
content.english: Lesson from the first book of Kings

content.latin: 51 Et perfécit omne opus, quod faciébat Sálomon in domo Dómini, et íntulit quæ sanctificáverat David pater suus, argéntum, et aurum, et vasa, reposuítque in thesáuris domus Dómini.
content.english: 51 And Solomon finished all the work that he made in the house of the Lord, and brought in the things that David his father had dedicated, the silver and the gold, and the vessels, and laid them up in the treasures of the house of the Lord.

content.latin: 1 Tunc congregáti sunt omnes maióres natu Israël cum princípibus tríbuum et duces familiárum filiórum Israël ad regem Salomónem in Ierúsalem, ut deférrent arcam fœ́deris Dómini de civitáte David, id est de Sion.
content.english: 1 Then all the ancients of Israel with the princes of the tribes, and the heads of the families of the children of Israel were assembled to king Solomon in Jerusalem: that they might carry the ark of the covenant of the Lord out of the city of David, that is, out of Sion.

content.latin: 2 Convenítque ad regem Salomónem univérsus Israël in mense Ethánim in solémni die (ipse est mensis séptimus).
content.english: 2 And all Israel assembled themselves to king Solomon on the festival day in the month of Ethanim, the same is the seventh month.

content.latin: ℣. Tu autem, Dómine, miserére nobis.
content.english: ℣. But thou, O Lord, have mercy upon us.

content.latin: ℟. Deo grátias.
content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

content.latin: ℟. Peccávi super númerum arénæ maris, et multiplicáta sunt peccáta mea: et non sum dignus vidére altitúdinem cæli præ multitúdine iniquitátis meæ: quóniam irritávi iram tuam,
content.english: ℟. My sins are many, yea, they are more in number than the sands of the sea; I am not worthy to look up toward heaven because of the multitude of my iniquities; for I have provoked thee to anger;

content.latin: * Et malum coram te feci.
content.english: * And done evil in thy sight.

content.latin: ℣. Quóniam iniquitátem meam ego cognósco: et delíctum meum contra me est semper, quia tibi soli peccávi.
content.english: ℣. For I acknowledge my transgression, and my sin is ever before me, for against thee only have I sinned.

content.latin: ℟. Et malum coram te feci.
content.english: ℟. And done evil in thy sight.

content.latin: ℣. Iube, Dómine, benedícere.
content.english: ℣. Grant, Lord, a blessing.

content.latin: Benedictio. Cuius festum cólimus, ipse intercédat pro nobis ad Dóminum.
content.english: Benediction. He whose feast-day we are keeping, be our Advocate with God.

content.latin: ℟. Amen.
content.english: ℟. Amen.

content.latin: 3 Venerúntque cuncti senes de Israël, et tulérunt arcam sacerdótes,
content.english: 3 And all the ancients of Israel came, and the priests took up the ark,

content.latin: 4 Et portavérunt arcam Dómini, et tabernáculum fœ́deris et ómnia vasa sanctuárii, quæ erant in tabernáculo, et ferébant ea sacerdótes et levítæ.
content.english: 4 And carried the ark of the Lord, and the tabernacle of the covenant, and all the vessels of the sanctuary, that were in the tabernacle: and the priests and the Levites carried them.

content.latin: 5 Rex autem Sálomon et omnis multitúdo Israël, quæ convénerat ad eum, gradiebátur cum illo ante arcam, et immolábant oves et boves absque æstimatióne et número.
content.english: 5 And king Solomon, and all the multitude of Israel, that were assembled unto him went with him before the ark, and they sacrificed sheep and oxen that could not be counted or numbered.

content.latin: 6 Et intulérunt sacerdótes arcam fœ́deris Dómini in locum suum, in oráculum templi, in Sanctum sanctórum, subter alas Chérubim;
content.english: 6 And the priests brought in the ark of the covenant of the Lord into its place, into the oracle of the temple, into the holy of holies under the wings of the cherubims.

content.latin: 7 Síquidem Chérubim expandébant alas super locum arcæ, et protegébant arcam, et vectes eius désuper.
content.english: 7 For the cherubims spread forth their wings over the place of the ark, and covered the ark, and the staves thereof above.

content.latin: 9 In arca autem non erat áliud nisi duæ tábulæ lapídeæ, quas posúerat in ea Móyses in Horeb, quando pépigit Dóminus fœdus cum fíliis Israël, cum egrederéntur de terra Ægýpti.

content.latin: Camíllus, Bucclánici in Theatínæ diœcésis óppido, ex nóbili Lelliórum família natus, adoléscens rem militárem secútus, sǽculi vítiis aliquámdiu indúlsit. Divínæ tamen offénsæ dolóre corréptus, ad fratres Minóres, quos Capuccínos vocant, cónvolans, ut eórum número adscriberétur, eníxe postulávit. Voti compos semel atque íterum factus, fœdo úlcere, quo aliquándo laboráverat, in eius tíbia iteráto recrudescénte, superiórum plácitis humíliter se submíttens, illíus religiónis bis expetítum et suscéptum hábitum bis dimísit. Romam proféctus, et sacerdótio rite initiátus, prima iecit fundaménta congregatiónis Clericórum regulárium infírmis ministrántium, sodálibus quarto obstríctis máxime árduo voto, infírmis, quos étiam pestis infecísset, ministrándi. Iterátis ieiúniis et assíduis fractus labóribus, quinque moléstis æque ac diútinis morbis, quos misericórdias Dómini appellábat, fórtiter tolerátis óbiit in Dómino, prídie idus iúlii, anno millésimo sexcentésimo décimo quarto, ætátis sexagésimo quinto. Eum Leo décimus tértius cæléstem ómnium hospitálium et infirmórum patrónum renuntiávit, eiúsque nomen in agonizántium litaníis invocári præcépit.
content.english: Camillus, of the noble family of the Lelli, was born at Bucchianico in the diocese of Chieti. As a young man he entered the army and gave himself up for a time to worldly vices. But he was seized with sorrow at having offended God, and, going at once to the Friars Minor, called Capuchins, he earnestly pleaded to be admitted among them. His desire was granted this time, and again later on, when he had been out of the Order and had sought re-admission. But on both occasions an infected ulcer on his leg, which had afflicted him for some time, broke out, and he submitted himself humbly to his superiors, twice putting off the habit of the Order which he had twice asked for and received. He went to Rome and was ordained to the priesthood. Then he laid the first foundations of the Congregation of Clerks Regular for ministering to the sick, whose members bind themselves by a fourth and difficult vow to serve the sick even when they are infected by the plague. Worn out by repeated fasts and constant toil, and by five long and trying illnesses which he called the mercies of the Lord and bore with great fortitude, he died in the Lord on the 14th of July, 1614, at the age of sixty-five. Leo XIII proclaimed him the heavenly patron of all hospitals and of the sick, and ordered that his name be invoked in the litany for the dying.

content.english: 36:6 That they may know thee, as we also have known thee, * that there is no God beside thee, O Lord.

content.latin: 36:7 Ínnova signa, et immúta mirabília. * Glorífica manum, et brácchium dextrum.
content.english: 36:7 Renew thy signs, and work new miracles. * Glorify thy hand, and thy right arm.

content.latin: 36:8 Éxcita furórem, et effúnde iram. * Tolle adversárium, et afflíge inimícum.
content.english: 36:8 Raise up indignation, and pour out wrath. * Take away the adversary, and crush the enemy.

content.latin: 36:9 Festína tempus, et meménto finis, * ut enárrent mirabília tua.
content.english: 36:9 Hasten the time, and remember the end, * that they may declare thy wonderful works.

content.latin: 36:10 In ira flammæ devorétur qui salvátur: * et qui péssimant plebem tuam, invéniant perditiónem.
content.english: 36:10 Let him that escapeth be consumed by the rage of the fire: * and let them perish that oppress thy people.

content.latin: 36:11 Cóntere caput príncipum inimicórum, * dicéntium: Non est álius præter nos.
content.english: 36:11 Crush the head of the princes of the enemies * that say: There is no other beside us.

content.latin: 36:12 Cóngrega omnes tribus Iacob: ut cognóscant quia non est Deus nisi tu, * et enárrent magnália tua:
content.english: 36:12 Gather together all the tribes of Jacob: that they may know that there is no God besides thee, * and may declare thy great works.

content.latin: 36:13 Et hereditábis eos, * sicut ab inítio.
content.english: 36:13 And thou shalt inherit them * as from the beginning.

content.latin: 36:14 Miserére plebi tuæ, super quam invocátum est nomen tuum: * et Israël, quem coæquásti primogénito tuo.
content.english: 36:14 Have mercy on thy people, upon whom thy name is invoked: * and upon Israel, whom thou hast raised up to be thy firstborn.

content.latin: 36:15 Miserére civitáti sanctificatiónis tuæ Ierúsalem, * civitáti requiéi tuæ.
content.english: 36:15 Have mercy on Jerusalem, the city which thou hast sanctified, * the city of thy rest.

content.latin: 36:16 Reple Sion inenarrabílibus verbis tuis, * et glória tua pópulum tuum.
content.english: 36:16 Fill Sion with thy unspeakable words, * and thy people with thy glory.

content.latin: Beátus vir, qui invéntus est sine mácula, et qui post aurum non ábiit, nec sperávit in pecúnia et thesáuris. Quis est hic, et laudábimus eum? fecit enim mirabília in vita sua.
content.english: Blessed is the rich man that is found without blemish: and that hath not gone after gold, nor put his trust in money nor in treasures. Who is he, and we will praise him? for he hath done wonderful things in his life.

content.latin: Iesu, coróna célsior,
content.english: Jesu, eternal truth sublime,

content.latin: Et véritas sublímior,
content.english: Through endless years the same!

content.latin: Qui confiténti sérvulo
content.english: Thou crown of those who through all time

content.latin: Reddis perénne prǽmium:
content.english: Confess thy holy name:

content.latin: Da supplicánti cœ́tui,
content.english: Thy suppliant people, through the prayer

content.latin: Huius rogátu, nóxii
content.english: Of thy blest saint, forgive;

content.latin: Remissiónem críminis,
content.english: For his dear sake, thy wrath forbear,

content.latin: Rumpéndo nexum vínculi.
content.english: And bid our spirits live.

content.latin: Anni revérso témpore,
content.english: Again returns the sacred day,

content.latin: Dies refúlsit lúmine,
content.english: With heavenly glory bright,

content.latin: Quo Sanctus hic de córpore
content.english: Which saw him go upon his way

content.latin: Migrávit inter sídera.
content.english: Into the realms of light.

content.latin: Hic vana terræ gáudia,
content.english: All objects of our vain desire,

content.latin: Et luculénta prǽdia,
content.english: All earthly joys and gains,

content.latin: Pollúta sorde députans,
content.english: To him were but as filthy mire;

content.latin: Ovans tenet cæléstia.
content.english: And now with thee he reigns.

content.latin: Te, Christe, Rex piíssime,
content.english: Thee, Jesu, his all-gracious Lord,

content.latin: Hic confiténdo iúgiter,
content.english: Confessing to the last,

content.latin: Calcávit artes dǽmonum,
content.english: He trod beneath him Satan's fraud,

content.latin: Sævúmque avérni príncipem.
content.english: And stood forever fast.

content.latin: Virtúte clarus, et fide,
content.english: In holy deeds of faith and love,

content.latin: Confessióne sédulus,
content.english: In fastings and in prayers,

content.latin: Ieiúna membra déferens,
content.english: His days were spent; and now above

content.latin: Dapes supérnas óbtinet.
content.english: Thy heavenly feast he shares.

content.latin: Proínde te piíssime
content.english: Then, for his sake thy wrath lay by,

content.latin: Precámur omnes súpplices:
content.english: And hear us while we pray;

content.latin: Nobis ut huius grátia
content.english: And pardon us, O thou most high,

content.latin: Pœnas remíttas débitas.
content.english: On this his festal day.

content.latin: Patri perénnis glória,
content.english: All glory to the Father be;

content.latin: Natóque Patris único,
content.english: And sole Incarnate Son;

content.latin: Sanctóque sit Paráclito,
content.english: Praise, holy Paraclete, to thee;

content.latin: Per omne semper sǽculum.
content.english: While endless ages run.

content.english: ℟. And showed him the kingdom of God.

content.latin: 1:68 Benedíctus ✠ Dóminus, Deus Israël: * quia visitávit, et fecit redemptiónem plebis suæ:
content.english: 1:68 Blessed be the Lord ✠ God of Israel; * because he hath visited and wrought the redemption of his people:

content.latin: 1:69 Et eréxit cornu salútis nobis: * in domo David, púeri sui.
content.english: 1:69 And hath raised up an horn of salvation to us, * in the house of David his servant:

content.latin: 1:70 Sicut locútus est per os sanctórum, * qui a sǽculo sunt, prophetárum eius:
content.english: 1:70 As he spoke by the mouth of his holy Prophets, * who are from the beginning:

content.latin: 1:71 Salútem ex inimícis nostris, * et de manu ómnium, qui odérunt nos.
content.english: 1:71 Salvation from our enemies, * and from the hand of all that hate us:

content.latin: 1:72 Ad faciéndam misericórdiam cum pátribus nostris: * et memorári testaménti sui sancti.
content.english: 1:72 To perform mercy to our fathers, * and to remember his holy testament,

content.latin: 1:73 Iusiurándum, quod iurávit ad Ábraham patrem nostrum, * datúrum se nobis:
content.english: 1:73 The oath, which he swore to Abraham our father, * that he would grant to us,

content.latin: 1:74 Ut sine timóre, de manu inimicórum nostrórum liberáti, * serviámus illi.
content.english: 1:74 That being delivered from the hand of our enemies, * we may serve him without fear,

content.latin: 1:75 In sanctitáte, et iustítia coram ipso, * ómnibus diébus nostris.
content.english: 1:75 In holiness and justice before him, * all our days.

content.latin: 1:76 Et tu, puer, Prophéta Altíssimi vocáberis: * præíbis enim ante fáciem Dómini, paráre vias eius:
content.english: 1:76 And thou, child, shalt be called the prophet of the Highest: * for thou shalt go before the face of the Lord to prepare his ways:

content.latin: 1:77 Ad dandam sciéntiam salútis plebi eius: * in remissiónem peccatórum eórum:
content.english: 1:77 To give knowledge of salvation to his people, * unto the remission of their sins:

content.latin: 1:78 Per víscera misericórdiæ Dei nostri: * in quibus visitávit nos, óriens ex alto:
content.english: 1:78 Through the bowels of the mercy of our God, * in which the Orient from on high hath visited us:

content.latin: 1:79 Illumináre his, qui in ténebris, et in umbra mortis sedent: * ad dirigéndos pedes nostros in viam pacis.
content.english: 1:79 To enlighten them that sit in darkness, and in the shadow of death: * to direct our feet into the way of peace.

content.latin: Deus, qui sanctum Camíllum, ad animárum in extrémo agóne luctántium subsídium, singulári caritátis prærogatíva decorásti: eius, quǽsumus, méritis, spíritum nobis tuæ dilectiónis infúnde; ut in hora éxitus nostri hostem víncere, et ad cæléstem mereámur corónam perveníre.
content.english: O God, Who, to succour the souls of the dying in their last agony, didst ennoble the holy Camillus with an extraordinary grace of charity, we beseech thee to pour into our hearts, for his sake, the Spirit of thy love, that we may worthily prevail against the enemy in the hour when we depart hence, and pass to receive a crown of glory in heaven.

content.english: Ant. Even the very hairs of your head are all numbered: fear not therefore; ye are of more value than many sparrows.

content.english: O God, who dost permit us to keep the birthday of thy holy Martyrs Symphorosa and her sons, grant that we may enjoy their fellowship in everlasting happiness.

content.english: Now in the sun's new dawning ray,

content.english: Lowly of heart, our God we pray

content.latin: Ut in diúrnis áctibus
content.english: That he from harm may keep us free

content.latin: Nos servet a nocéntibus.
content.english: In all the deeds this day shall see.

content.latin: Linguam refrénans témperet,
content.english: May fear of him our tongues restrain,

content.latin: Ne litis horror ínsonet:
content.english: Lest strife unguarded speech should stain:

content.latin: Visum fovéndo cóntegat,
content.english: His favouring care our guardian be,

content.latin: Ne vanitátes háuriat.
content.english: Lest our eyes feed on vanity.

content.latin: Sint pura cordis íntima,
content.english: May every heart be pure from sin

content.latin: Absístat et vecórdia;
content.english: And folly find no place therein:

content.latin: Carnis terat supérbiam
content.english: Scant need of food, excess denied,

content.latin: Potus cibíque párcitas.
content.english: Wear down in us the body's pride.

content.latin: Ut, cum dies abscésserit,
content.english: That when the light of day is gone,

content.latin: Noctémque sors redúxerit,
content.english: And night in course shall follow on.

content.latin: Mundi per abstinéntiam
content.english: We, free from cares the world affords,

content.latin: Ipsi canámus glóriam.
content.english: May chant the praise that is our Lord's.

content.english: All laud to God the Father be,

content.latin: Eiúsque soli Fílio,
content.english: All praise, Eternal Son, to thee:

content.latin: Cum Spíritu Paráclito,
content.english: All glory, as is ever meet,

content.latin: Nunc et per omne sǽculum.
content.english: To God the holy Paraclete.

content.english: Ant. Lift up thyself, O Lord, * thou that judgest the earth: render retribution to the proud.

content.latin: 93:1 Deus ultiónum Dóminus: * Deus ultiónum líbere egit.
content.english: 93:1 The Lord is the God to whom revenge belongeth: * the God of revenge hath acted freely.

content.latin: 93:2 Exaltáre, qui iúdicas terram: * redde retributiónem supérbis.
content.english: 93:2 Lift up thyself, thou that judgest the earth: * render a reward to the proud.

content.latin: 93:3 Úsquequo peccatóres, Dómine, * úsquequo peccatóres gloriabúntur:
content.english: 93:3 How long shall sinners, O Lord: * how long shall sinners glory?

content.latin: 93:4 Effabúntur, et loquéntur iniquitátem: * loquéntur omnes, qui operántur iniustítiam?
content.english: 93:4 Shall they utter, and speak iniquity: * shall all speak who work injustice?

content.latin: 93:5 Pópulum tuum, Dómine, humiliavérunt: * et hereditátem tuam vexavérunt.
content.english: 93:5 Thy people, O Lord, they have brought low: * and they have afflicted thy inheritance.

content.latin: 93:6 Víduam, et ádvenam interfecérunt: * et pupíllos occidérunt.
content.english: 93:6 They have slain the widow and the stranger: * and they have murdered the fatherless.

content.latin: 93:7 Et dixérunt: Non vidébit Dóminus, * nec intélleget Deus Iacob.
content.english: 93:7 And they have said: The Lord shall not see: * neither shall the God of Jacob understand.

content.latin: 93:8 Intellégite, insipiéntes in pópulo: * et stulti, aliquándo sápite.
content.english: 93:8 Understand, ye senseless among the people: * and, you fools, be wise at last.

content.latin: 93:9 Qui plantávit aurem, non áudiet? * aut qui finxit óculum, non consíderat?
content.english: 93:9 He that planted the ear, shall he not hear? * or he that formed the eye, doth he not consider?

content.latin: 93:10 Qui córripit gentes, non árguet: * qui docet hóminem sciéntiam?
content.english: 93:10 He that chastiseth nations, shall he not rebuke: * he that teacheth man knowledge?

content.latin: 93:11 Dóminus scit cogitatiónes hóminum, * quóniam vanæ sunt.
content.english: 93:11 The Lord knoweth the thoughts of men, * that they are vain.

content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: 93:12 Beátus homo, quem tu erudíeris, Dómine: * et de lege tua docúeris eum,
content.english: 93:12 Blessed is the man whom thou shalt instruct, O Lord: * and shalt teach him out of thy law.

content.latin: 93:13 Ut mítiges ei a diébus malis: * donec fodiátur peccatóri fóvea.
content.english: 93:13 That thou mayst give him rest from the evil days: * till a pit be dug for the wicked.

content.latin: 93:14 Quia non repéllet Dóminus plebem suam: * et hereditátem suam non derelínquet.
content.english: 93:14 For the Lord will not cast off his people: * neither will he forsake his own inheritance.

content.latin: 93:15 Quoadúsque iustítia convertátur in iudícium: * et qui iuxta illam omnes qui recto sunt corde.
content.english: 93:15 Until justice be turned into judgment: * and they that are near it are all the upright in heart.

content.latin: 93:16 Quis consúrget mihi advérsus malignántes? * aut quis stabit mecum advérsus operántes iniquitátem?
content.english: 93:16 Who shall rise up for me against the evildoers? * or who shall stand with me against the workers of iniquity?

content.latin: 93:17 Nisi quia Dóminus adiúvit me: * paulo minus habitásset in inférno ánima mea.
content.english: 93:17 Unless the Lord had been my helper, * my soul had almost dwelt in hell.

content.latin: 93:18 Si dicébam: Motus est pes meus: * misericórdia tua, Dómine, adiuvábat me.
content.english: 93:18 If I said: My foot is moved: * thy mercy, O Lord, assisted me.

content.latin: 93:19 Secúndum multitúdinem dolórum meórum in corde meo: * consolatiónes tuæ lætificavérunt ánimam meam.
content.english: 93:19 According to the multitude of my sorrows in my heart, * thy comforts have given joy to my soul.

content.latin: 93:20 Numquid adhǽret tibi sedes iniquitátis: * qui fingis labórem in præcépto?
content.english: 93:20 Doth the seat of iniquity stick to thee, * who framest labour in commandment?

content.latin: 93:21 Captábunt in ánimam iusti: * et sánguinem innocéntem condemnábunt.
content.english: 93:21 They will hunt after the soul of the just, * and will condemn innocent blood.

content.latin: 93:22 Et factus est mihi Dóminus in refúgium: * et Deus meus in adiutórium spei meæ.

content.latin: 107:6 Exaltáre super cælos, Deus, et super omnem terram glória tua: * ut liberéntur dilécti tui.
content.english: 107:6 Be thou exalted, O God, above the heavens, and thy glory over all the earth: * that thy beloved may be delivered.

content.latin: 107:7 Salvum fac déxtera tua, et exáudi me: * Deus locútus est in sancto suo:

content.latin: 107:8 Exsultábo, et dívidam Síchimam, * et convállem tabernaculórum dimétiar.
content.english: 107:8 I will rejoice, and I will divide Sichem * and I will mete out the vale of tabernacles.

content.latin: 107:9 Meus est Gálaad, et meus est Manásses: * et Éphraim suscéptio cápitis mei.
content.english: 107:9 Galaad is mine: and Manasses is mine: * and Ephraim the protection of my head.

content.latin: 107:10 Iuda rex meus: * Moab lebes spei meæ.
content.english: 107:10 Juda is my king: * Moab the pot of my hope.

content.latin: 107:10 In Idumǽam exténdam calceaméntum meum: * mihi alienígenæ amíci facti sunt.
content.english: 107:10 Over Edom I will stretch out my shoe: * the aliens are become my friends.

content.latin: 107:11 Quis dedúcet me in civitátem munítam? * quis dedúcet me usque in Idumǽam?
content.english: 107:11 Who will bring me into the strong city? * who will lead me into Edom?

content.latin: 107:12 Nonne tu, Deus, qui repulísti nos, * et non exíbis, Deus, in virtútibus nostris?
content.english: 107:12 Wilt not thou, O God, who hast cast us off? * and wilt not thou, O God, go forth with our armies?

content.latin: 107:13 Da nobis auxílium de tribulatióne: * quia vana salus hóminis.
content.english: 107:13 O grant us help from trouble: * for vain is the help of man.

content.english: 107:14 Through God we shall do mightily: * and he will bring our enemies to nothing.

content.latin: Colóssis, in Phrýgia, natális sancti Epaphræ, quem sanctus Paulus Apóstolus concaptívum appéllat. Hic, ab eódem Apóstolo Colóssis Epíscopus ordinátus, ibídem, clarus virtútibus, martýrii palmam, pro óvibus sibi commendátis, viríli agóne percépit; cuius corpus Romæ, in Basílica sanctæ Maríæ Maióris, cónditum est.
content.english: The holy Epaphras, whom the holy Apostle Paul doth call his own fellow prisoner. He was ordained by the same Apostle Bishop of Colossi, where, illustrious for graces, he gained the palm of martyrdom in manly contending on behalf of the sheep committed to his care. His body is buried at Rome, in the Church of St Mary the greater.

content.latin: Tréviris sancti Martíni, Epíscopi et Mártyris.
content.english: At Seville, in Spain, the holy Virgins Justa and Rufina. They were arrested under the President Diogenian. They were first racked and tormented by being torn with hooks, and afterwards afflicted with imprisonment, starvation, and diverse tortures. In the end Justa gave up the ghost in prison, and Rufina had her neck broken for confessing the Lord, [at the end of the third century.]

content.latin: Híspali, in Hispánia, pássio sanctárum Vírginum Iustæ et Rufínæ, quæ, a Prǽside Diogeniáno comprehénsæ, primo equúlei extensióne et ungulárum laniatióne vexátæ, póstea cárcere, inédia et váriis torsiónibus sunt afflíctæ; tandem Iusta in cárcere spíritum exhalávit, Rufínæ vero cervix, in confessióne Dómini, confrácta est.
content.english: At Cordova, the holy Virgin Aurea, who for a time fell away, but repented of what she had done, and in a renewed combat prevailed against the enemy by the shedding of her blood, [in the year 856.]

content.latin: Córdubæ, in Hispánia, sanctæ Aureæ Vírginis, beatórum Adúlphi et Ioánnis Mártyrum soróris; quæ aliquándo in apostasíæ crimen a Mahumetáno Iúdice indúcta est, sed mox, facti pǽnitens, iteráto certámine, hostem effúso sánguine superávit.
content.english: At Trier, the holy martyr Martin, Bishop [of that see, in the year 210.]

content.latin: Romæ sancti Sýmmachi Papæ, qui, a schismaticórum factióne diútius fatigátus, demum, sanctitáte conspícuus, migrávit ad Dóminum.
content.english: At Rome, the holy Pope Symmachus, who long suffered through the deeds of the schismatics, and at length passed away, famous for holiness, to be ever with the Lord, [in the year 514.]

content.english: 101:4 For my days are vanished like smoke: * and my bones are grown dry like fuel for the fire.

content.latin: 101:5 Percússus sum ut fænum, et áruit cor meum: * quia oblítus sum comédere panem meum.
content.english: 101:5 I am smitten as grass, and my heart is withered: * because I forgot to eat my bread.

content.latin: 101:6 A voce gémitus mei * adhǽsit os meum carni meæ.
content.english: 101:6 Through the voice of my groaning, * my bone hath cleaved to my flesh.

content.latin: 101:7 Símilis factus sum pellicáno solitúdinis: * factus sum sicut nyctícorax in domicílio.
content.english: 101:7 I am become like to a pelican of the wilderness: * I am like a night raven in the house.

content.latin: 101:8 Vigilávi, * et factus sum sicut passer solitárius in tecto.
content.english: 101:8 I have watched, * and am become as a sparrow all alone on the housetop.

content.latin: 101:9 Tota die exprobrábant mihi inimíci mei: * et qui laudábant me, advérsum me iurábant.

content.latin: 101:11 A fácie iræ et indignatiónis tuæ: * quia élevans allisísti me.

content.english: 101:15 For the stones thereof have pleased thy servants: * and they shall have pity on the earth thereof.

content.latin: 101:16 Et timébunt gentes nomen tuum, Dómine, * et omnes reges terræ glóriam tuam.
content.english: 101:16 And the Gentiles shall fear thy name, O Lord, * and all the kings of the earth thy glory.

content.latin: 101:17 Quia ædificávit Dóminus Sion: * et vidébitur in glória sua.
content.english: 101:17 For the Lord hath built up Sion: * and he shall be seen in his glory.

content.latin: 101:18 Respéxit in oratiónem humílium: * et non sprevit precem eórum.
content.english: 101:18 He hath had regard to the prayer of the humble: * and he hath not despised their petition.

content.latin: 101:19 Scribántur hæc in generatióne áltera: * et pópulus, qui creábitur, laudábit Dóminum:
content.english: 101:19 Let these things be written unto another generation: * and the people that shall be created shall praise the Lord:

content.latin: 101:20 Quia prospéxit de excélso sancto suo: * Dóminus de cælo in terram aspéxit:
content.english: 101:20 Because he hath looked forth from his high sanctuary: * from heaven the Lord hath looked upon the earth.

content.latin: 101:21 Ut audíret gémitus compeditórum: * ut sólveret fílios interemptórum:
content.english: 101:21 That he might hear the groans of them that are in fetters: * that he might release the children of the slain:

content.latin: 101:22 Ut annúntient in Sion nomen Dómini: * et laudem eius in Ierúsalem.
content.english: 101:22 That they may declare the name of the Lord in Sion: * and his praise in Jerusalem;

content.latin: 101:23 In conveniéndo pópulos in unum, * et reges ut sérviant Dómino.
content.english: 101:23 When the people assemble together, * and kings, to serve the Lord.

content.latin: ℣. Glória Patri, et Fílio, * et Spirítui Sancto.
content.english: ℣. Glory be to the Father, and to the Son, * and to the Holy Ghost.

content.latin: ℟. Sicut erat in princípio, et nunc, et semper, * et in sǽcula sæculórum. Amen.
content.english: ℟. As it was in the beginning, is now, * and ever shall be, world without end. Amen.

content.latin: 101:24 Respóndit ei in via virtútis suæ: * Paucitátem diérum meórum núntia mihi.
content.english: 101:24 He answered him in the way of his strength: * Declare unto me the fewness of my days.

content.latin: 101:25 Ne révoces me in dimídio diérum meórum: * in generatiónem et generatiónem anni tui.
content.english: 101:25 Call me not away in the midst of my days: * thy years are unto generation and generation.

content.latin: 101:26 Inítio tu, Dómine, terram fundásti: * et ópera mánuum tuárum sunt cæli.
content.english: 101:26 In the beginning, O Lord, thou foundedst the earth: * and the heavens are the works of thy hands.

content.latin: 101:27 Ipsi períbunt, tu autem pérmanes: * et omnes sicut vestiméntum veteráscent.
content.english: 101:27 They shall perish but thou remainest: * and all of them shall grow old like a garment:

content.latin: 101:28 Et sicut opertórium mutábis eos, et mutabúntur: * tu autem idem ipse es, et anni tui non defícient.
content.english: 101:28 And as a vesture thou shalt change them, and they shall be changed. * But thou art always the selfsame, and thy years shall not fail.

content.latin: 101:29 Fílii servórum tuórum habitábunt: * et semen eórum in sǽculum dirigétur.
content.english: 101:29 The children of thy servants shall continue: * and their seed shall be directed for ever.

content.latin: Ant. Clamor meus, Dómine, ad te pervéniat: non avértas fáciem tuam a me.
content.english: Ant. Let my cry reach unto thee, O Lord: turn not away thy face from me.

content.latin: Beátus vir, qui invéntus est sine mácula, et qui post aurum non ábiit, nec sperávit in pecúnia et thesáuris. Quis est hic, et laudábimus eum? fecit enim mirabília in vita sua.
content.english: Blessed is the rich man that is found without blemish: and that hath not gone after gold, nor put his trust in money nor in treasures. Who is he, and we will praise him? for he hath done wonderful things in his life.

content.english: ℟. Thanks be to God.

content.latin: Deus, qui sanctum Camíllum, ad animárum in extrémo agóne luctántium subsídium, singulári caritátis prærogatíva decorásti: eius, quǽsumus, méritis, spíritum nobis tuæ dilectiónis infúnde; ut in hora éxitus nostri hostem víncere, et ad cæléstem mereámur corónam perveníre.
content.english: O God, Who, to succour the souls of the dying in their last agony, didst ennoble the holy Camillus with an extraordinary grace of charity, we beseech thee to pour into our hearts, for his sake, the Spirit of thy love, that we may worthily prevail against the enemy in the hour when we depart hence, and pass to receive a crown of glory in heaven.

content.english: Alleluia.

content.latin: Rector potens, verax Deus,
content.english: O God of truth, O Lord of might,

content.latin: Qui témperas rerum vices,
content.english: Who orderest time and change aright,

content.latin: Splendóre mane illúminas,
content.english: Who send’st the early morning ray,

content.latin: Et ígnibus merídiem:
content.english: And light’st the glow of perfect day:

content.latin: Exstíngue flammas lítium,
content.english: Extinguish thou each sinful fire,

content.latin: Aufer calórem nóxium,
content.english: And banish every ill desire;

content.latin: Confer salútem córporum,
content.english: And while thou keep’st the body whole,

content.latin: Verámque pacem córdium.
content.english: Shed forth thy peace upon the soul.

content.latin: Præsta, Pater piíssime,
content.english: Almighty Father, hear our cry,

content.latin: Patríque compar Únice,
content.english: Through Jesus Christ, our Lord most High,

content.latin: Cum Spíritu Paráclito
content.english: Who, with the Holy Ghost and thee,

content.latin: Regnans per omne sǽculum.
content.english: Doth live and reign eternally.
